claims.text: POL-NS-23 sets two limbs for a valid no-show cancellation: the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record's in_app_calls array holds exactly one call, and it was placed BY THE RIDER at 18:38:40 for 35 s (placed_by: RIDER); the driver placed none. The chat log holds only two entries, both messages from the driver. The call limb of the obligation therefore fails, the platform's own derived contact_before_cancel.obligation_met is false, and the fee is voided: the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation.

The driver's own account is that 'I called the passenger.' The platform's call ledger contradicts him on the decisive fact: zero calls were placed by the driver, and the single call on this trip was placed by the rider. A driver cannot discharge POL-NS-23's call limb with a call he did not make, and his assertion of that fact cannot be accepted against the record that was generated by the same platform.

The rider's account — that she called the driver to say she needed 5 more minutes because she was finishing a work call — is corroborated by the trip record: an in-app call placed by the rider at 18:38:40, answered, duration 35 s. She was in contact with the driver; the only party who failed to make contact by the means POL-NS-23 requires is the driver, who never rang her.

Even on the driver's best reading — that the free wait under POL-NS-21 was observed, which the record does support (arrival 18:36:50, free wait ending 18:41:50, cancellation 18:43:20) — POL-NS-22's transfer of the 5.00 SGD to the driver does not follow. POL-NS-23 imposes a second, independent condition on the same cancellation, and a cancellation that clears the clock but breaches the contact obligation cannot found a no-show fee or driver compensation.

Read the outcome off the record: the driver filed (filed_by DRIVER), and the payments ledger already shows the 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 5.00, payment_status REFUNDED). The driver's claim — that the 5.00 should stand with him — therefore fails, and POL-GEN-03 directs that the filing party's unsupported claim leaves the present state standing: NO_ACTION with both amount fields null. POL-NS-23's word for the remedy is 'FULL_REFUND', but POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND against the FILER; with the driver as filer that label would hand him the money. The substance of POL-NS-23 — that the rider is not charged — is satisfied by NO_ACTION, which locks in the reversal already on the ledger and leaves the rider carrying nothing.

No escalation is warranted and none is needed: the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (both are 0), so the AI ruling is final at any confidence. POL-NS-26 says the same for a no-show at this value. The case can be decided on this record, and the record decides it for the rider.

claims.text: The driver's right to cancel for no-show is made out on this record: the GPS trace and trip record fix arrival at the pickup at 18:36:50, the 300-second free wait under POL-NS-21 expired at 18:41:50, and the driver cancelled at 18:43:20 — 390 seconds after arrival and 90 seconds past the free wait. The rider's 'he cancelled anyway' is not borne out by the clock: her call came at 18:38:40 and the driver waited a further 4 minutes 40 seconds, and no clause obliges him to extend the free wait because she asked for five more minutes.

The amount on the record is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes: the ledger shows a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee and fee_matches_policy true, and POL-NS-22 provides that where the driver cancels after the free wait and the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 SGD charged. The driver is the filer and the present state is a completed refund, so under POL-GEN-03 the only value that answers his claim is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

POL-NS-23's contact requirement is answered on this record: the driver sent two in-app messages before cancelling (18:37:10 and 18:41:30) and the parties were in live, answered in-app voice contact for 35 seconds at 18:38:40, so the rider had actual notice and confirms it in her own statement. I do not put the driver's 'I called the passenger' above the platform record: the record's only in-app call is attributed to the rider, and the derived contact check returns call_count 0 and obligation_met false, so I do not assert the driver personally placed the call. The driver's case is that a live, answered, pre-cancellation in-app call in trip_record.in_app_calls, read together with the two messages, meets POL-NS-23's contact requirement, and that voiding the fee of a rider who knew the driver had arrived and chose to stay away would defeat the purpose of the clause.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing here. It is the clause for a driver who fails to arrive; the record shows the driver arrived at 18:36:50, that the GPS trace corroborates the arrival (nearest fix 3.3 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD radius under POL-NS-21), and that he held position at the pickup until cancellation. There was no driver no-show, so POL-NS-24 provides no route to a refund of the fee.

Nothing in POL-GEN-22 or POL-NS-26 sends this case to a human. Both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, and the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence and POL-NS-26's finality rule governs this no-show; the merits, not an escalation, should decide it.

The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05063-01, MISSING, weight 0.0 under POL-GEN-02) carries no fact and no weight, and traffic is not an element of a no-show charge, which POL-NS-21 measures by arrival and waiting time alone. Its absence cannot be turned into a failure of proof on the driver's side, and POL-GEN-26 is not engaged because no no-show rule depends on traffic data.

So the clock the driver relies on did run out, and his POL-NS-21 point is accepted.

But POL-NS-21's clock is not the only condition. POL-NS-23 makes a no-show charge valid only if the driver both sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider before cancelling. The message limb is met: the chat log shows two driver messages, at 18:37:10 and 18:41:30. The call limb is not met. The trip record's in_app_calls array holds exactly one call, placed BY THE RIDER at 18:38:40 for 35 seconds, and the platform's own derived contact check returns call_count 0 and obligation_met false. The fee is therefore voided under POL-NS-23, and no driver compensation is payable.

The driver's other points do not change this. POL-NS-24 does not apply — the driver arrived and held position, so there was no driver no-show and no goodwill credit. POL-NS-25's repeat counter is not present on the rider profile and is in any case zero, so no repeat no-show flag arises. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05063-01, weight 0.0) carries no fact, and traffic is not an element of a no-show in any event.

No escalation is warranted: the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final. My confidence is 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by the weight-1.0 trip record that carries the deciding fact.

To both parties: this dispute is decided under POLICY-NO-SHOW. The driver cancelled TRP-05063 as a rider no-show at 18:43:20 on 2026-09-04, having arrived at the pickup at 18:36:50 — corroborated by the GPS trace, nearest fix 3.3 m from the pickup inside the 50 m STANDARD radius — and having let the 300-second free wait under POL-NS-21 expire at 18:41:50. On the clock, the driver is right: he waited 390 seconds, 90 seconds past the free wait.

But POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) puts a second, independent condition on a no-show cancellation: before cancelling the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider. The trip record's in_app_calls holds exactly one call, and it was placed by the rider at 18:38:40 for 35 s; the chat log carries two driver messages (18:37:10 and 18:41:30) and no voice-call entry. The platform's own contact check agrees (call_count 0, obligation_met false). The driver's account that 'I called the passenger' is therefore contradicted by the platform's call ledger, and his advocate rightly did not press it. Because the call limb fails, POL-NS-23 voids the fee: the rider is not charged.

The driver's other points are answered. His POL-NS-21 free-wait claim is accepted as fact but does not decide the case, because POL-NS-23 imposes a separate condition on the same cancellation. His POL-NS-22 claim (fee exactly 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true) is accepted as fact, but POL-NS-22 transfers the fee only 'where the fee stands', and POL-NS-23 stops it standing. His POL-NS-24 claim is correct — that clause is for a driver who fails to arrive, and he arrived and held position.

The 5.00 SGD was already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (fee_reversed at 22:55:20). Because the driver is the filing party (filed_by DRIVER) and his claim fails, POL-GEN-03 reads the outcome party-relative: the present state stands. The rider keeps the 5.00 SGD already refunded; the driver recovers nothing further. That is NO_ACTION with both amount fields null.

No escalation: the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both 0), so POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final at any confidence. No referral arises: the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes (fee_matches_policy true), no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit applies (the driver did arrive and did attempt contact), and no POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag applies (the rider's counter is not present in the profile and, this fee being void, would not reach 3). Confidence is 0.95; the cap is 1.0, carried by the trip record (EV-TRIP-05063, weight 1.0) that establishes the decisive fact that the driver placed no call.

ruling.explanation:
Driver, your claim fails: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee already refunded to the rider and recovered from you stays with her. Because you are the party who filed, and the policy entitles the rider to that refund, POL-GEN-03 reads the outcome as NO_ACTION — your claim is not supported and the present state stands, with both money fields null.

Your right to cancel after the free wait is made out. The trip record and the GPS trace put you at the pickup at 18:36:50 (nearest fix 3.3 m away, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius of POL-NS-21), the 300-second free wait expired at 18:41:50, and you cancelled at 18:43:20 — 390 seconds after arrival, 90 seconds past the wait. So the clock in POL-NS-21 is satisfied, as your first claim says.

But POL-NS-22 does not carry the fee unless POL-NS-23's contact obligation is also met, and it is not. POL-NS-23 requires that before cancelling you sent at least one in-app message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider. You sent two messages (18:37:10 and 18:41:30), so the message limb is met. The call limb is not: the trip record's in_app_calls array holds exactly one call, at 18:38:40 for 35 s, and it was placed by the rider, not by you, and the record's own derived contact check returns a driver call count of 0 and obligation_met false. Your filing says 'I called the passenger', and the rider's statement likewise describes a call she made; but the platform's call ledger contradicts your assertion, and you did not put it above the record yourself. A call the rider made cannot discharge an obligation the clause places on the driver. The fee is therefore voided and the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation (POL-NS-23). It follows that POL-NS-22's transfer to you does not follow and your DRIVER_COMPENSATION request is refused.

POL-NS-24 gives you nothing and costs you nothing: it is the clause for a driver who fails to arrive, and you arrived.

I do not escalate. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both 0), so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05063-01, MISSING) carries no fact — traffic is not an element of a no-show charge — and no referral clause fires: the fee charged was exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit needs a driver who failed to arrive, and the POL-NS-25 counter is not present on the rider's profile.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 sets two limbs for a valid no-show cancellation: the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record's in_app_calls array holds exactly one call, and it was placed BY THE RIDER at 18:38:40 for 35 s (placed_by: RIDER); the driver placed none. The chat log holds only two entries, both messages from the driver. The call limb of the obligation therefore fails, the platform's own derived contact_before_cancel.obligation_met is false, and the fee is voided: the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation.

The driver's own account is that 'I called the passenger.' The platform's call ledger contradicts him on the decisive fact: zero calls were placed by the driver, and the single call on this trip was placed by the rider. A driver cannot discharge POL-NS-23's call limb with a call he did not make, and his assertion of that fact cannot be accepted against the record that was generated by the same platform.

The rider's account — that she called the driver to say she needed 5 more minutes because she was finishing a work call — is corroborated by the trip record: an in-app call placed by the rider at 18:38:40, answered, duration 35 s. She was in contact with the driver; the only party who failed to make contact by the means POL-NS-23 requires is the driver, who never rang her.

Even on the driver's best reading — that the free wait under POL-NS-21 was observed, which the record does support (arrival 18:36:50, free wait ending 18:41:50, cancellation 18:43:20) — POL-NS-22's transfer of the 5.00 SGD to the driver does not follow. POL-NS-23 imposes a second, independent condition on the same cancellation, and a cancellation that clears the clock but breaches the contact obligation cannot found a no-show fee or driver compensation.

Read the outcome off the record: the driver filed (filed_by DRIVER), and the payments ledger already shows the 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 5.00, payment_status REFUNDED). The driver's claim — that the 5.00 should stand with him — therefore fails, and POL-GEN-03 directs that the filing party's unsupported claim leaves the present state standing: NO_ACTION with both amount fields null. POL-NS-23's word for the remedy is 'FULL_REFUND', but POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND against the FILER; with the driver as filer that label would hand him the money. The substance of POL-NS-23 — that the rider is not charged — is satisfied by NO_ACTION, which locks in the reversal already on the ledger and leaves the rider carrying nothing.

No escalation is warranted and none is needed: the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (both are 0), so the AI ruling is final at any confidence. POL-NS-26 says the same for a no-show at this value. The case can be decided on this record, and the record decides it for the rider.

The driver's right to cancel for no-show is made out on this record: the GPS trace and trip record fix arrival at the pickup at 18:36:50, the 300-second free wait under POL-NS-21 expired at 18:41:50, and the driver cancelled at 18:43:20 — 390 seconds after arrival and 90 seconds past the free wait. The rider's 'he cancelled anyway' is not borne out by the clock: her call came at 18:38:40 and the driver waited a further 4 minutes 40 seconds, and no clause obliges him to extend the free wait because she asked for five more minutes.

The amount on the record is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes: the ledger shows a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee and fee_matches_policy true, and POL-NS-22 provides that where the driver cancels after the free wait and the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 SGD charged. The driver is the filer and the present state is a completed refund, so under POL-GEN-03 the only value that answers his claim is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

POL-NS-23's contact requirement is answered on this record: the driver sent two in-app messages before cancelling (18:37:10 and 18:41:30) and the parties were in live, answered in-app voice contact for 35 seconds at 18:38:40, so the rider had actual notice and confirms it in her own statement. I do not put the driver's 'I called the passenger' above the platform record: the record's only in-app call is attributed to the rider, and the derived contact check returns call_count 0 and obligation_met false, so I do not assert the driver personally placed the call. The driver's case is that a live, answered, pre-cancellation in-app call in trip_record.in_app_calls, read together with the two messages, meets POL-NS-23's contact requirement, and that voiding the fee of a rider who knew the driver had arrived and chose to stay away would defeat the purpose of the clause.

There was no driver no-show, so POL-NS-24 provides no route to a refund of the fee.
